title: The Hypocrisy of Steam
author: HereToLearn321
selftext:
I will never understand the point of view of those who are totally against AI art but totally cool with AI code/engineering.

So hypocritical. Just because a few coders in the world invented this technology doesn't mean it is not "stealing" code from many devs that oppose AI.

Sure many devs are now using AI because they are FORCED to do it or are faced with being unemployed.





I get if you are totally cool with everyone using AI for anything, and also if you oppose ALL ai, not just the stuff you personally like doing or care about. That seems logical to me and congruent. Otherwise it seems hypocritical.



It is quite surprising Steam took the hypocritical stance. And that so few people are calling them out on it. Seems the big corps get a free pass on their stance or use of AI.  Only the little small game devs get crucified.

comments.author: xcdesz
comments.body:
Steam seems fine with either AI art or AI code, but you just have to disclose.  They wont enforce AI code because its impossible to prove.

I think the AI art bad, AI code good hypocrisy is because modern software development for the last 25 years is mostly built around the benefits of open source and sharing code, and developers have seen it working in practice without threatening their jobs and paychecks.   Artists have always been more protective and mistrusting when it comes to sharing, and havent embraced the concept like software folks have.  I get that they are different things, but Im overall of the opinion that sharing leads to growth, and the art community could learn from the programmers on this concept.

comments.author: erratic_ostrich
comments.body:
The logic is that art by definition is what humans do to express themselves, so it must be done by a human to qualify as art. Code just needs to work, doesn't need to express anything.

Personally I think complaining about any of this is fucking retarded, but the distinction between art and code is quite clear.

Regarding the stealing, AI learned mostly from documentation and publicly available repos, the same a human could do without qualifying as stealing. If you never shared your code, AI didn't learn from it.

And what you call being FORCED to use AI it's normally called having a job, the same way fast food employes are FORCED to flip burgers and so on. Any programmer who is not willingly keeping up with the latest tech should look into another career

replies.author: Komondor_Interactive
replies.body: You can't compare humans learning from open source stuff and machines scraping the whole internet illegally without respecting licensing for billionaires to create a product

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Not illegally, not breaking any license. As I said before, the code used for learning was willingly shared.

And I don't want to sound dismissive but I'm not willing to discuss billonaries and capitalism, it has nothing to do with the topic of this post... An open source llm hosted locally by an non-wealthy person  can scrap the whole internet and learn from it too, is there any difference?

replies.author: Komondor_Interactive
replies.body:
Bruh, I never agreed when posting on Stackoverflow Reddit or YouTube comments to train these AIs, you can't scrap websites like it's the damn far west, there are rules and they didn't respect any of them. They didn't, and not only for code, it's the same for books, films, music, podcasts, ect ect... Same with GitHub, a lot of open source project are non-commercial, which means you can't create a product with it ( which AI company did ), or there are licenses that says you must credit them if you use them ( which AI companies did not ).. they also, and it's more and more clear, decompile softwares to make the AIs learn from it, which is also illegal.
So yes it was made absolutely illegally. By the way there are many AI models that are trained legally and ethically, so it means it's not impossible.

Capitalism may have nothing to do with the post, but everything with how AI was created and also who it does profit for.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
You also never agreed to having humans learning from your reddit posts, but that doesn't make it illegal.

You can't create commercial products from some open source repos and/or must credit the author if you use them, but there's no law against learning from it.

Ethically, it is debatable, I don't agree but I do see your point.  
Legally, you just got it wrong, that's not how it works... There were many specific cases where they overstepped the law (specially in the early days of training) and they got properly sued for it, we'll see more of those cases over time. But the standard method of scrapping data is always done within what's legally allowed, otherwise they would've been sued into bankrupcy long ago

replies.author: Komondor_Interactive
replies.body:
- Yes I absolutely did agree on this mister because I made it public for other humans. It is the very basic of Internet, sharing something with other human so they can read/see it, learn from it and/or interact with you. Not for it being scraped, tho. I, for example didn't agree for other humans to learn from my private messages. But Meta did train their LLMs on that too apparently..

- But AI is still not "learning like a human" hell it does not even work like a human brain, stop comparing both. It's a huge web scraping, not "learning". If it is, then a python script that scraps your whole Facebook profile is also just "learning". What's the difference ? This is a term used by AI companies to normalize what they did but it is absolutely not comparable by just how it works. Also, I seriously consider people who want to give the same rights to AI than to human to be brain damaged psychopats ( sorry if it is your case )..

- They are already sued by multiple companies, and the vaste majority just started recently. So it will be a looooooong time before anything happens. Also, it is way harder to prove that you copied some code than if you copied a book or music. And don't forget that GitHub collaborated with AI companies, so it makes everything even worse.
Btw, I'm speaking about a European perspective, might be different in America.

comments.author: Beginning-Wear-3017
comments.body:
Just because AI models are trained on public code doesn’t mean it’s “stealing.” Code has always been about sharing and collaboration, if you didn’t want it shared, you kept it private.   
  
Publicly available code online has always been meant to be reused under the terms of its license. That’s the foundation of open source: building on each other’s work.

Comparing this to AI art is misleading. In software, reusing and remixing code is part of the culture and ecosystem; in art, originality and authorship carry a different weight. Pretending they’re the same thing ignores decades of how developers have actually worked.   
  
So stop acting like you understand coding culture when you clearly don’t.

comments.author: NicNacksTheSixSnax
comments.body:
There’s nothing wrong with AI code for anything. 

Pre-AI if I wanted code for a character controller, scene, function, or anything else I’d just copy/paste from someone else (stackOverflow) and modify for my own purposes.

AI simplifies that because I no longer have to spend hours searching for answers and can just build. 

anti-AI folks kill me with this argument that using AI makes people’s work “less than.” It’s the equivalent argument to saying people who started using nail guns instead of hammers ruined Carpentry. 

A poorly made game that used AI is a poorly made game.   
A well made game that used AI is a well made game. 

End of story.
